mcqs.question:
Two draft posters about a health camp are shown below.
Poster A reads: "Join the Health Camp – Your Body Deserves the Best Care – Register Today!"
Poster B reads: "Health Camp. Date: 5th June. Venue: Community Hall."
Which poster demonstrates stronger persuasive language?
mcqs.explanation: Poster A employs imperative verbs ("Join", "Register"), an emotive appeal ("Your Body Deserves the Best Care"), and a clear call‑to‑action, all of which are hallmarks of persuasive language. Poster B merely presents factual information without any persuasive elements.

mcqs.question:
Which revision of the following line best maintains clarity and brevity for a poster announcing a book fair?
Original: "We are delighted to inform all the students of the school that a grand book fair will be organized in the school auditorium on the 12th of July, and everyone is encouraged to participate and explore a wide variety of books."

options.A: Grand book fair on 12 July in school auditorium. All students invited to explore many books.
options.B: The school will hold a book fair on July 12th in the auditorium. Students may attend.
options.D: Students are invited to a book fair on July 12th at the school auditorium, featuring many books.

mcqs.answer: The school will hold a book fair on July 12th in the auditorium. Students may attend.
mcqs.explanation: Option B conveys the essential information (what, when, where, who) in a clear, concise sentence without unnecessary words. Option A, while brief, still contains extra phrasing; C is overly terse and may omit needed context; D is longer than necessary.

mcqs.question: Why is it important to identify the purpose and audience before designing a poster?

options.A: To choose appropriate language, visuals, and layout that suit the intended readers
options.B: To decide the poster's size only

mcqs.answer: To choose appropriate language, visuals, and layout that suit the intended readers
mcqs.explanation: Knowing the purpose (inform, persuade, invite, etc.) and the target audience (students, parents, general public) guides every design decision—choice of words, images, colour, and hierarchy—ensuring the poster is effective. The other options are peripheral considerations.

mcqs.question: Which of the following headings would be most effective for a poster aimed at encouraging students to volunteer for a community clean‑up?

options.B: Help Keep Our Neighborhood Clean – Volunteer Today!

mcqs.answer: Help Keep Our Neighborhood Clean – Volunteer Today!
mcqs.explanation: Option B combines a clear call‑to‑action ("Volunteer Today!") with a benefit‑oriented message ("Help Keep Our Neighborhood Clean"), making it both attention‑grabbing and persuasive. The other headings are either too vague or lack an imperative appeal.

mcqs.question: In the context of poster writing, "select relevant information" means:

options.A: Including every detail you know about the topic
options.B: Adding only facts and messages that directly support the poster’s purpose
options.C: Using long paragraphs to explain background

mcqs.answer: Adding only facts and messages that directly support the poster’s purpose
mcqs.explanation: Relevant information is that which advances the poster’s main objective—whether to inform, persuade, or invite. Extraneous details (options A, C, D) clutter the design and dilute the message.

mcqs.question: Which sentence best uses persuasive language for a poster promoting a school sports day?

options.A: Sports day will be held on 20th March.
options.B: Come and showcase your talent at the school sports day – be a champion!
options.C: The school organizes a sports day annually.
options.D: Students may attend the sports day if they wish.

mcqs.answer: Come and showcase your talent at the school sports day – be a champion!
mcqs.explanation: Option B employs an enthusiastic invitation, action verbs ("Come", "showcase"), and a motivational phrase ("be a champion"), all of which are persuasive. The other options are neutral statements lacking persuasive appeal.

mcqs.question: Consider the following poster excerpt: "SAVE WATER – TURN OFF TAPS WHEN NOT IN USE. EVERY DROP COUNTS." Which feature most clearly illustrates clarity and brevity?

options.B: Short, direct command with limited words

mcqs.answer: Short, direct command with limited words
mcqs.explanation: The message conveys the essential action and its importance in just a few words, exemplifying both clarity (easy to understand) and brevity (concise). Visual styling (A, C) and word choice (D) support the message but do not define brevity.

mcqs.question: A school wants to create a poster to invite parents to a parent‑teacher meeting scheduled on 10th September at 5 pm in the school auditorium. The poster will be displayed on the school notice board. What should be identified as the primary purpose and the target audience for this poster?

options.A: Purpose: advertise school events; Audience: students
options.B: Purpose: inform about meeting details; Audience: parents

mcqs.answer: Purpose: inform about meeting details; Audience: parents
mcqs.explanation: The main goal is to convey the date, time, and venue of the parent‑teacher meeting, so the purpose is informational. The intended readers are the parents of students, making them the target audience. The other options misstate either purpose or audience.
